title: rhus toxicodendron subsp. radicans
intro: Rhus toxicodendron subsp. radicans, commonly known as Poison Ivy, is a perennial shrub native to North America, characterized by its highly irritating sap, which causes skin inflammation and blisters upon contact. Despite its toxic properties, the plant has been traditionally used in herbal medicine for its health benefits, including reducing inflammation, relieving pain, and treating skin conditions such as eczema and acne. The therapeutic actions of Poison Ivy are attributed to its ability to modulate the immune system, reduce oxidative stress, and exhibit anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. The bioactive constituents responsible for these effects include triterpenoid saponins, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which have been shown to possess antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant activities.
